The absolutely continuous part of a positive current need not be closed. It is therefore useful to impose a determinant bound on all positive currents first, and only afterwards select a current with the prescribed cohomology class. Lebesgue decompositions below are taken with respect to any smooth positive volume form; the absolutely continuous and singular parts are independent of that choice. Lemma 10.97.1 . u $ be a smooth strictly positive volume form. Suppose that for every Gauduchon metric $\chi $ there is a positive real $(1,1)$-current $\xi _\chi $ such that F1F6EF454245 10.97.5  egin{equation}  (\xi _{\chi ,\mathrm{ac}})^ n\geq 
u \quad 	ext{almost everywhere}, \qquad \int _ X\xi _{\chi ,\mathrm{ac}}\wedge \chi ^{n-1} \leq \int _ X\psi \wedge \chi ^{n-1}. \end{equation} Then there is a positive closed current $R=\psi +dd^ cu$ with $u$ a real distribution and BDB8ECE5CC82 10.97.6  egin{equation}  (R_{\mathrm{ac}})^ n\geq 
u \quad 	ext{almost everywhere}. \end{equation} The auxiliary currents $\xi _\chi $ may depend on $\chi $ and need not be closed. No Kähler hypothesis is required. Proof. Use the real locally convex space of real $(1,1)$-currents, with the weak topology defined by smooth real $(n-1,n-1)$-forms. Let \[  \mathcal C=\mathcal C_
u , \qquad \mathcal F=\{ \psi +dd^ cu:u	ext{ is a real distribution on }X\} .  \] The set $\mathcal C$ is nonempty: a sufficiently large multiple of any Hermitian metric belongs to it. It is convex and weakly closed by lemma 10.97.1 . We also use the distributional potential argument in the proof of the Gauduchon criterion for positivity . That argument establishes, for arbitrary real currents, not just positive ones, that the image of $dd^ c$ on real distributions is the annihilator of the smooth real $(n-1,n-1)$-forms $\Gamma $ satisfying $dd^ c\Gamma =0$. The image is therefore weakly closed, so $\mathcal F$ is a weakly closed affine subspace. This is the Bott–Chern class of $\psi $; because $\psi $ is closed, every member of $\mathcal F$ is closed. Choose one Gauduchon metric $\chi _0$, using the conformal Gauduchon representative , and put $\Gamma _0=\chi _0^{n-1}$. Integration by parts gives 891A615E98CC 10.97.7  egin{equation}  \langle S,\Gamma _0angle =\langle \psi ,\Gamma _0angle \qquad (S\in \mathcal F). \end{equation} The strict positivity of $\Gamma _0$ means that bounds for this pairing control all coefficient masses of a positive current on the compact manifold. Assume that $\mathcal C\cap \mathcal F$ is empty. The convex set $\mathcal D=\mathcal C-\mathcal F$ then does not contain zero. We claim that $\mathcal D$ is weakly closed. Indeed, let a net $W_ a=T_ a-S_ a\in \mathcal D$ tend weakly to $W$. By ( 10.97.7 ), \[  \langle T_ a,\Gamma _0angle =\langle W_ a+\psi ,\Gamma _0angle  \] is eventually bounded. Weak compactness of positive currents with bounded mass supplies a subnet on which $T_ aightharpoonup T$. Here $T\in \mathcal C$ by weak closedness. On this subnet, $S_ a=T_ a-W_ aightharpoonup T-W\in \mathcal F$, so $W\in \mathcal D$. Strict Hahn–Banach separation of the closed convex set $\mathcal D$ from zero gives a smooth real $(n-1,n-1)$-form $\sigma $ and $c>0$ satisfying AF202F866E29 10.97.8  egin{equation}  \langle T-S,\sigma angle \geq c \qquad (T\in \mathcal C,\  S\in \mathcal F). \end{equation} Replacing $S$ by $S+tdd^ cv$ for arbitrary real $t$ and arbitrary real distribution $v$ shows that $dd^ c\sigma =0$. Replacing $T$ by $T+tV$ for arbitrary positive current $V$ and $t\geq 0$ shows that $\langle V,\sigma angle \geq 0$. Thus $\sigma $ is semipositive. For $\varepsilon >0$, put $\sigma _\varepsilon =\sigma +\varepsilon \Gamma _0$. It is strictly positive and $dd^ c$-closed. Uniformly over $T\in \mathcal C$, \[  \langle T-\psi ,\sigma _\varepsilon angle \geq c-\varepsilon \langle \psi ,\Gamma _0angle .  \] Choose $\varepsilon $ so small that the right side is at least $c/2$; if $\langle \psi ,\Gamma _0angle \leq 0$, any positive sufficiently small $\varepsilon $ works. The smooth positive root construction in the Gauduchon criterion for positivity gives a Hermitian metric $\chi $ with $\chi ^{n-1}=\sigma _\varepsilon $; it is Gauduchon because $dd^ c\sigma _\varepsilon =0$. Use the current $\xi _\chi $ from ( 10.97.5 ). Its absolutely continuous part itself belongs to $\mathcal C$, although it need not be closed. Substitution of $T=\xi _{\chi ,\mathrm{ac}}$ yields \[  \int _ X\xi _{\chi ,\mathrm{ac}}\wedge \chi ^{n-1} -\int _ X\psi \wedge \chi ^{n-1}\geq c/2,  \] contradicting the hypothesis. Hence $\mathcal C\cap \mathcal F$ is nonempty, and any current in that intersection has the required properties. $\square$ Remark 10.97.9 . D0CFC4418A8D The positivity used in the convex set is essential, whereas closedness of its members would be inappropriate: the final contradiction uses an absolutely continuous part. Closedness is imposed by the affine space $\mathcal F$. Likewise, the hypothesis only compares one trace for each test metric; it does not compare the currents $\xi _\chi $ to one another.

title: 13.31 Absolutely continuous and non-pluripolar mass
text:
Lemma 13.31.1 (Absolutely continuous mass and non-pluripolar mass) . C7894CAD8593 Let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on a complex manifold of dimension $n\geq 1$. Suppose that $\langle T^ nangle $ is locally finite. Write $T_{\mathrm{ac}}$ for the absolutely continuous part of its coefficient measures, with respect to local Lebesgue measure. Its coefficients form a measurable positive semidefinite Hermitian matrix almost everywhere. Then \[  (T_{\mathrm{ac}})^ n\leq \langle T^ nangle  \] as measures. The left side means the pointwise exterior power of this measurable tensor; no closedness of $T_{\mathrm{ac}}$ is asserted. In particular, if $X$ is compact Kähler and $T\in \alpha $, then \[  \int _ X(T_{\mathrm{ac}})^ n\leq \operatorname {Vol}(\alpha ),  \] where volume is the positive top intersection number defined by non-pluripolar mass. Proof. We first record the small measure-theoretic extension of Lebesgue differentiation needed below. If $\mu $ is a locally finite complex Radon measure on a Euclidean domain and $\mu =f\, \mathrm dx+\mu _ s$ is its Lebesgue decomposition, then, for a smooth nonnegative compactly supported mollifier $ho $ of integral one, 58A08DA1A586 13.31.2  egin{equation}  \mu *ho _ r\longrightarrow f \quad \hbox{almost everywhere as }r\downarrow 0. \end{equation} This is local, so multiply $\mu $ by a compactly supported cutoff equal to one on a neighborhood of the compact set under consideration. title: 10.98 Transcendental Morse inequalities
text: We use the cohomological volume defined by positive intersection products. The comparison in lemma 13.31.1 , together with the class mass bound, gives the following useful way of estimating it: 60E6DED87465 10.98.1 \begin{equation}  \operatorname {Vol}(a)\geq \int _ X(T_{\mathrm{ac}})^ n \qquad (T\in a,\quad T\geq 0\text{ closed}). \end{equation} The inequality below uses this cohomological volume. Theorem 10.98.2 . DE32EEA596CD Let $X$ be a compact connected Kähler manifold of dimension $n\geq 1$, and let $a,b\in H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb R)$ be nef. Then 74CB0E2B99CA 10.98.3 \begin{equation}  \operatorname {Vol}(a-b) \geq a^ n-n\, a^{n-1}\cdot b. \end{equation} Here the right side consists of ordinary cohomological intersections, and the volume is zero outside the pseudoeffective cone. If the right side is strictly positive, $a-b$ is big. Proof. The assertion is immediate if $X$ is empty, so assume $X$ is nonempty. First suppose $n\geq 2$ and that $a,b$ are Kähler classes. Choose Kähler representatives $\gamma \in a$ and $\eta \in b$, and write \[  A=\int _ X\gamma ^ n, \qquad C=\int _ X\gamma ^{n-1}\wedge \eta , \qquad \delta =\frac{nC}{A}.  \] Both $A$ and $C$ are strictly positive. If $\delta \geq 1$, the desired lower bound is nonpositive and follows from the nonnegativity of volume. We may therefore assume $0<\delta <1$. The null-support construction and its regularization, theorem 5.64.2 , corollary 5.64.4 , give a closed positive current $T\in b$ with continuous potential and support in a closed Lebesgue-null set $\Sigma $, and smooth Kähler forms $T_ k\in b$ converging weakly to $T$. Choose decreasing open neighborhoods $U_ j$ of $\Sigma $ with $\overline U_{j+1}\subset U_ j$ and $\bigcap _ j\overline U_ j=\Sigma $. Choose $0\leq \rho _ j\leq 1$ smooth with $\operatorname {supp}\rho _ j\subset U_ j$ and $\rho _ j=1$ on $U_{j+1}$. Fix a Gauduchon metric $\chi $, and put \[  B=\int _ X\eta \wedge \chi ^{n-1}>0.  \] The trace identity and the support of $T$ give \[  \int _ X\rho _ jT\wedge \chi ^{n-1} =\int _ XT\wedge \chi ^{n-1}=B.  \] For each $j$, choose a sufficiently large index $k(j)$ such that, after passing to an increasing choice of indices, FE1FC41D41AE 10.98.4 \begin{equation}  m_ j:=\int _{U_ j}T_{k(j)}\wedge \chi ^{n-1}\geq B-j^{-1}. \end{equation} For brevity write $\tau _ j=T_{k(j)}$. All these choices may depend on $\chi $. The smooth Monge–Ampère theorem, smooth Hermitian Monge–Ampère existence , applied with closed background $\gamma $, yields a Kähler form $\gamma _ j\in a$ satisfying BE76273E23F2 10.98.5 \begin{equation}  \gamma _ j^ n=(1-\delta )\gamma ^ n +\frac{\delta A}{B}\tau _ j\wedge \chi ^{n-1}. \end{equation} Indeed, the right side is smooth and strictly positive and has integral $A$, since the Gauduchon trace of $\tau _ j\in b$ equals $B$. The scalar normalization in that theorem is consequently zero for the closed background, by Stokes' theorem. We next estimate the trace of $\gamma _ j$ on the same small set $U_ j$. At each point, let $0<\lambda _1\leq \cdots \leq \lambda _ n$ be its eigenvalues relative to $\tau _ j$. Put $q_ j=(\tau _ j\wedge \chi ^{n-1})/\tau _ j^ n$ and $P_ j=\lambda _2\cdots \lambda _ n$. Then \[  \gamma _ j\geq \lambda _1\tau _ j, \qquad \lambda _1P_ j\geq \frac{\delta A}{B}q_ j,  \] and therefore 08054B9DCC9E 10.98.6 \begin{equation}  \int _{U_ j}\gamma _ j\wedge \chi ^{n-1} \geq \frac{\delta A}{B} \int _{U_ j}\frac{q_ j^2}{P_ j}\, \tau _ j^ n. \end{equation} Cauchy–Schwarz, followed by the elementary mixed-wedge identity, gives \[  m_ j^2 \leq \left(\int _{U_ j}\frac{q_ j^2}{P_ j}\, \tau _ j^ n\right) \left(\int _{U_ j}P_ j\, \tau _ j^ n\right), \qquad P_ j\tau _ j^ n\leq n\gamma _ j^{n-1}\wedge \tau _ j.  \] The last form is positive, so its integral on $U_ j$ is at most its integral on $X$, namely $nC$, because both factors are closed and remain in the fixed classes $a,b$. Since $\delta A=nC$, we obtain 58B9EC1F5AF1 10.98.7 \begin{equation}  \int _{U_ j}\gamma _ j\wedge \chi ^{n-1} \geq \frac{m_ j^2}{B}\geq B-\frac{2}{j} \end{equation} once $j>B^{-1}$. The constant and this threshold are allowed to depend on the fixed test metric; the determinant lower bound below will not. The positive currents $\gamma _ j$ have bounded mass, because their Kähler cohomology class is fixed. After passing to a subsequence, let $\gamma _ j\rightharpoonup \xi _\chi $, a closed positive current in $a$. To locate its trace mass, fix $k$ and take $j>k$. Since $\rho _ k=1$ on $U_ j$, ( 10.98.7 ) gives \[  \int _ X\rho _ k\gamma _ j\wedge \chi ^{n-1}\geq B-2/j.  \] First pass to the weak limit in $j$, then let $k\to \infty $. The cutoffs converge pointwise to the indicator of $\Sigma $; dominated convergence for the finite trace measure yields \[  \int _\Sigma \xi _\chi \wedge \chi ^{n-1}\geq B.  \] The absolutely continuous part assigns no mass to $\Sigma $. Hence 1BAC4BA78448 10.98.8 \begin{equation}  \int _ X\xi _{\chi ,\mathrm{sing}}\wedge \chi ^{n-1}\geq B, \qquad \int _ X\xi _{\chi ,\mathrm{ac}}\wedge \chi ^{n-1} \leq \int _ X(\gamma -\eta )\wedge \chi ^{n-1}. \end{equation} Only this trace inequality is asserted; it is not an inequality between $\xi _{\chi ,\mathrm{sing}}$ and $T$ as currents. On the other hand, ( 10.98.5 ) implies $\gamma _ j^ n\geq (1-\delta )\gamma ^ n$. The weak closedness established in lemma 10.97.1 therefore gives CBD8309C9C77 10.98.9 \begin{equation}  (\xi _{\chi ,\mathrm{ac}})^ n\geq (1-\delta )\gamma ^ n \quad \text{almost everywhere}. \end{equation} The right side is strictly positive and independent of $\chi $. Apply proposition 10.97.4 with $\psi =\gamma -\eta $ and $\nu =(1-\delta )\gamma ^ n$. Equations ( 10.98.8 ) and ( 10.98.9 ) provide its hypotheses for every Gauduchon metric. The resulting positive closed current $R\in a-b$ satisfies \[  (R_{\mathrm{ac}})^ n\geq (1-\delta )\gamma ^ n.  \] Integrating and using ( 10.98.1 ) proves ( 10.98.3 ) for Kähler classes. For nef $a,b$, fix a Kähler class $w$ and apply the result just proved to $a+\varepsilon w$ and $b+\varepsilon w$. Their difference is exactly $a-b$, so the left side does not vary. Letting $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$ only uses continuity of the intersection polynomial on the right. In particular, this step does not assume continuity of volume. For $n=1$, a real $(1,1)$-class on the compact connected curve is determined by its integral. The scalar Green operator represents every zero-integral smooth form as $dd^ c$ of a smooth function, by global complex Hessian potentials . It follows that a class of nonnegative integral has a smooth nonnegative representative and volume equal to that integral, while a class of negative integral is not pseudoeffective and has volume zero. Thus the asserted inequality reads $\max \{ a-b,0\} \geq a-b$ for the numerical degrees and is immediate. Finally, a strictly positive lower bound for volume gives bigness by the positive-mass bigness criterion, bigness and positive non-pluripolar volume . $\square$

title: 13.32 Numerical positive products
text: Throughout, $X$ is a nonempty connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n\geq 1$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. We use $dd^ c=\mathrm i\partial \bar\partial /(2\pi )$, and all products of singular currents are non-pluripolar products. Write $V_\theta $ for the normalized potential with minimal singularities in the big class $\alpha =\{ \theta \} $, and set $\operatorname {Vol}(\alpha )=\int _ X\langle \theta _{V_\theta }^ n\rangle $. For pseudo-effective classes the volume is defined by decreasing Kähler perturbations, as in positive mixed intersection numbers . Lemma 13.32.1 (Strict gentle approximation of a minimal potential) . B89CF500D374 For every big $\alpha =\{ \theta \} $ there are potentials $a_ j$ with gentle rational analytic singularities such that $\theta _{a_ j}$ is a Kähler current and $a_ j\to V_\theta $ in $d_{S,\theta }$. Proof. Choose a Kähler current $\theta _ v\geq \delta \omega $ in $\alpha $. Minimality permits a constant shift making $v\leq V_\theta $. For integers $l>1$, put $z_ l=(1-l^{-1})V_\theta +l^{-1}v$. These potentials increase almost everywhere to $V_\theta $, and $\theta _{z_ l}\geq (\delta /l)\omega $. By increasing multiplier-ideal envelopes , increasing continuity in the singularity metric , increasing multiplier envelopes and increasing $d_ S$ continuity give \[  P_\theta [z_ l]_{\mathcal I}\longrightarrow V_\theta \quad \hbox{in }d_{S,\theta }.  \] Here $P_\theta [V_\theta ]_{\mathcal I}=V_\theta $: the minimal potential is a normalized competitor for this envelope and dominates every normalized $\theta $-psh competitor, even before the multiplier condition is imposed. For fixed $l$, apply gentle quasi-equisingular approximation to $z_ l$ with background $\theta -(\delta /l)\omega $. On a tail its currents in background $\theta $ are at least $(\delta /2l)\omega $. The strict-current argument in the proof of analytic approximation of multiplier-ideal-good singularities shows that this quasi-equisingular sequence converges in $d_{S,\theta }$ to $P_\theta [z_ l]_{\mathcal I}$, without assuming that $z_ l$ is $\mathcal I$-good. The chosen regularization has gentle analytic singularities, so its residual on a resolution is smooth. Choose one member $a_ l$ at distance below $1/l$ from this multiplier envelope. The triangle inequality proves the asserted convergence. $\square$ Lemma 13.32.2 (Simultaneous exceptional correction) . 85B840A3A734 Let $\pi :Y\to X$ be a finite composite of smooth-center blowups. There is an effective rational exceptional divisor $F$ and a Kähler form $\gamma $ in $\pi ^*\{ \omega \} -\{ F\} $. If finitely many smooth closed forms satisfy $S_ i\geq \delta _ i\pi ^*\omega $, with $\delta _ i>0$, then \[  S_{i,t}=S_ i+t(\gamma -\pi ^*\omega )  \] are Kähler for $0<t\leq \min _ i\delta _ i$, and their classes are $\{ S_ i\} -t\{ F\} $. Any fixed finite list of their mixed intersection numbers, including intersections with fixed smooth pulled-back forms, converges to the corresponding uncorrected list as $t\downarrow 0$. Proof. For one blowup Kähler metrics on smooth-center blowups gives a Kähler class $\pi ^*\{ \omega \} -q\{ E\} $ for every sufficiently small $q>0$; choose $q$ rational. Inductively pull back the divisor already chosen and add a sufficiently small positive rational multiple of the new exceptional divisor. Pullback preserves effectiveness, and the same blowup construction preserves a Kähler representative. Isomorphism steps add nothing. For the identity map take $F=0$, $\gamma =\omega $. Now $S_{i,t}\geq (\delta _ i-t)\pi ^*\omega +t\gamma >0$. Each claimed integral is a polynomial in $t$, so finite simultaneous control follows by taking one sufficiently small positive rational $t$. No bound uniform over all modifications is asserted or used. $\square$ Theorem 13.32.3 (Same-class simultaneous approximation with finite tests) . AD36F0CA2A0B Let $\alpha _1,\ldots ,\alpha _ r$ be big classes, and let $\eta _1,\ldots ,\eta _ N$ be fixed smooth closed real $(1,1)$-forms. There are finite smooth-center modifications $\pi _ j:Y_ j\to X$, Kähler forms $\kappa _{i,j}$, and effective rational divisors $E_{i,j}$ such that \[  \pi _ j^*\alpha _ i=A_{i,j}+\{ E_{i,j}\} ,\qquad A_{i,j}=\{ \kappa _{i,j}\} .  \] Every top mixed intersection, with repetitions, converges to the mixed mass of currents with minimal singularities in the corresponding classes. Moreover, for every $(i_1,\ldots ,i_{n-1})$ and every $b$, \[  \int _{Y_ j}\kappa _{i_1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \kappa _{i_{n-1},j} \wedge \pi _ j^*\eta _ b \longrightarrow \int _ X\langle T_{i_1,\min }\wedge \cdots \wedge T_{i_{n-1},\min }\rangle \wedge \eta _ b.  \] For $n=1$ the latter expression means the empty product $1$; it is already unchanged under a modification. Proof. For each $i$, choose the strict gentle sequence of the first lemma in a fixed smooth representative $\theta _ i$ of $\alpha _ i$. For top mixed masses their convergence follows from continuity of mixed masses in the singularity metric . To obtain each additional test, choose $C_ b$ so large that $C_ b\omega +\eta _ b$ is Kähler, and write $\eta _ b=(C_ b\omega +\eta _ b)-C_ b\omega $. Use continuity of mixed masses in the singularity metric again with the final entry the fixed smooth potential $0$ in each of these two Kähler backgrounds. All backgrounds in these applications are big, as required. There are finitely many tests and index tuples, so one common diagonal selection suffices. Apply principalization of a coherent ideal successively to all chosen gentle ideal types, retaining the accumulated boundary divisor. This produces a common smooth-center modification on which \[  \pi _ j^*\theta _{i,a_{i,j}}=S_{i,j}+[B_{i,j}],  \] where $B_{i,j}$ is effective rational and $S_{i,j}$ is smooth. By gentle analytic singularities , the residual is smooth on a resolution of each ideal; it remains smooth under the later pullbacks. Off the divisor strictness implies $S_{i,j}\geq \delta _{i,j}\pi _ j^*\omega $ for some $\delta _{i,j}>0$; smoothness extends this inequality across the divisor. By the local calculus of non-pluripolar products , non-pluripolar products under modifications , locality, divisorial removal and modification invariance identify every uncorrected mixed integral with the corresponding downstairs non-pluripolar mixed mass. Smooth densities charge no divisor. Apply the preceding correction lemma on this common model. Choose a positive rational $t_ j\leq \min _ i\delta _{i,j}$ so small that every top integral and every listed test changes by less than $1/j$. The class identities are exact, while all claimed limits follow from the diagonal convergence and this error bound. In particular no curvature margin, exceptional coefficient or intersection polynomial is assumed uniformly bounded in $j$. $\square$ Definition 13.32.4 (The movable class in bidimension one) . 9CAC26397732 For big classes $\alpha _1,\ldots ,\alpha _{n-1}$ set \[  \langle \alpha _1\cdots \alpha _{n-1}\rangle =\{ \langle T_{1,\min }\wedge \cdots \wedge T_{n-1,\min }\rangle \}  \in H^{n-1,n-1}(X,\mathbb R).  \] For $n=1$, the definition is the class of $1$ in $H^{0,0}$. Proposition 13.32.5 (Numerical cofinality and movability) . 37818757E0D6 The preceding class is independent of the chosen minimal currents. One can choose the same-class approximations so that, simultaneously, \[  A_{i,j}^ n\longrightarrow \operatorname {Vol}(\alpha _ i),\qquad (\pi _ j)_*(A_{i_1,j}\cdots A_{i_{n-1},j}) \longrightarrow \langle \alpha _{i_1}\cdots \alpha _{i_{n-1}}\rangle .  \] The latter limit is in cohomology, not an assertion of monotonicity or convergence of particular current representatives. It belongs to the closed cone $\mathcal M$ generated by pushforwards of products of Kähler forms on modifications. More precisely, for every Kähler class $\beta $, pairing the movable class with $\beta $ is the supremum of the corresponding mixed nef-model intersections with $\pi ^*\beta $, over simultaneous decompositions $\pi ^*\alpha _ i=A_ i+\{ E_ i\} $ with $A_ i$ Kähler and $E_ i$ effective rational. The analogous supremum of $A^ n$ equals $\operatorname {Vol}(\alpha )$. Proof. By mass comparison for bounded singularity differences , bounded-type mixed-mass invariance, with one final smooth Kähler factor, makes every pairing with a Kähler class independent of the minimal representatives. Kähler classes span $H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb R)$: for any smooth closed real $\eta $, both $C\omega +\eta $ and $C\omega $ are Kähler for sufficiently large $C$. By Hodge theory and integration duality for a flat bundle , the real Kähler Hodge decomposition , the complementary-type Poincaré pairing is nondegenerate and the cohomology spaces are finite dimensional. These identifications also hold for closed currents: extend the Green operators to distributions by duality and transpose their identities, obtaining $S=\Pi S+\mathrm d(\mathrm d^*GS)$ for a closed current $S$, with $\Pi S$ smooth harmonic. Thus the pairing proves independence of the cohomology class. Choose finitely many smooth closed $\eta _ b$ representing a basis of $H^{1,1}$. The finite-test theorem proves the displayed convergence; each approximant belongs to the generating set of $\mathcal M$, so closedness gives membership in $\mathcal M$. For any admissible model let $R_ i=\pi _*(\kappa _ i+[E_ i])$. Its class is $\alpha _ i$, and it is closed positive. On the isomorphism locus of $\pi $, removing the divisors in the non-pluripolar product identifies its mixed product with that of the $\kappa _ i$. These currents have no mass on the excluded analytic set: downstairs this is the non-pluripolar property, and upstairs the trace against $\pi ^*\beta $ is a smooth density giving every analytic set zero mass. Thus their total mixed mass against $\beta $ equals $\int _ Y\kappa _1\cdots \kappa _{n-1}\pi ^*\beta $. The minimal-current bound of the positive mixed-mass bound puts this below the claimed pairing. The finite-test construction, with $\beta $ included, attains the bound in the limit. The same argument in top degree proves the volume supremum. This is cofinality for the relevant numerical suprema; no claim that the sequence eventually dominates each divisorial singularity type is needed. $\square$ Proposition 13.32.6 (Order and boundary limits) . B28D656FB542 Pairings of $\langle \alpha _1\cdots \alpha _{n-1}\rangle $ with a fixed Kähler class are nonnegative, homogeneous in each argument, superadditive in each argument, and increase when a pseudo-effective class is added to any argument. The class-valued product is continuous on the product of big cones. For pseudo-effective classes it has the well-defined extension \[  \langle \alpha _1\cdots \alpha _{n-1}\rangle =\lim _{\varepsilon \downarrow 0} \langle (\alpha _1+\varepsilon \{ \omega \} )\cdots (\alpha _{n-1}+\varepsilon \{ \omega \} )\rangle .  \] The limit is independent of the perturbing Kähler class, agrees with the big definition, and lies in $\mathcal M$. Boundary convergence is asserted for these decreasing Kähler perturbations; arbitrary continuity at every boundary point is not asserted. Proof. Nonnegativity, homogeneity and pseudo-effective order follow from the positive mixed-mass bound , choosing the reference Kähler metric to represent the test class. Superadditivity follows by adding two minimal currents in the replaced argument: the minimal current of the sum class has at least their mixed mass, and multilinearity expands that mass into the two original terms. Fix a big class $\alpha $ with $\alpha -\delta \{ \omega \} $ pseudo-effective, $\delta >0$. If $\beta \to \alpha $, finite-dimensional form comparison gives $-\varepsilon \{ \omega \} \leq \beta -\alpha \leq \varepsilon \{ \omega \} $ in pseudo-effective order, with $\varepsilon \to 0$. For $\varepsilon <\delta $ this implies \[  (1-\varepsilon /\delta )\alpha \leq \beta \leq (1+\varepsilon /\delta )\alpha .  \] Indeed $(\varepsilon /\delta )\alpha -\varepsilon \{ \omega \} $ is pseudo-effective. Apply these bounds in every argument and use homogeneity and order. Each pairing with a fixed Kähler class is squeezed between factors tending to $1$ times its value at the original tuple. A finite Kähler spanning family proves cohomological continuity. At the boundary these pairings decrease as $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$ and are nonnegative, so they have finite limits. A finite Kähler basis defines the limiting class, and every other pairing converges by linearity. Two Kähler forms satisfy $c^{-1}\omega \leq \omega '\leq c\omega $ for some $c>0$; the same order squeeze proves independence of the perturbation, including different fixed positive coefficients in different arguments. For big tuples the already proved continuity gives agreement. Finally $\mathcal M$ is closed and contains every big perturbation. $\square$

Then \[  \mathcal E=C^*,\qquad C=\mathcal E^*=\mathcal M.  \] If $\xi \notin \mathcal E$, there is an actual single-power generator with $\xi \cdot \mu _*(\kappa ^{n-1})<0$. Proof. A positive current $T\in \xi \in \mathcal E$ pulls back under a modification to a closed positive current: pull back local plurisubharmonic potentials, which are not identically minus infinity because the modification is an isomorphism on a nonempty open set. Pairing $\mu ^*T$ with any smooth mixed Kähler product and using the projection formula gives a nonnegative number. Thus $\mathcal E\subset C^*$ and $\mathcal M\subset \mathcal E^*$. Suppose $\xi \notin \mathcal E$ and fix a Kähler $\omega $. Since $\mathcal E$ is closed and adding a large multiple of $\omega $ makes a class Kähler, there is a threshold $t_0>0$ such that $\alpha =\xi +t_0\omega \in \partial \mathcal E$ and $\alpha +s\omega $ is big for every $s>0$. Here $\mathcal B=\operatorname {int}\mathcal E$: a strict current stays strict under small smooth class perturbations; conversely an interior class remains pseudoeffective after subtracting a small Kähler class, and adding that form to its positive current gives a strict current. Since $\alpha $ is not big, $\operatorname {vol}(\alpha )=0$. Put $\gamma _ s=P(\alpha +s\omega )$. The approximation in theorem 13.32.3 makes $\gamma _ s$ a limit of actual single-power generators, so $\gamma _ s\in C$. Also $\omega \cdot \gamma _ s>0$: monotonicity compares it with $s^{n-1}\omega ^ n>0$ (for $n=1$ the factor is $1$). For $0<\delta <\varepsilon $, the derivative formula of theorem 10.99.8 and monotonicity of the Kähler test pairing give \[  \operatorname {vol}(\alpha +\varepsilon \omega ) -\operatorname {vol}(\alpha +\delta \omega ) =n\int _\delta ^\varepsilon \omega \cdot \gamma _ s\, \mathrm ds \leq n(\varepsilon -\delta )\omega \cdot \gamma _\varepsilon .  \] Let $\delta \downarrow 0$ using the perturbation limit and zero boundary volume. By theorem 10.99.11 , \[  \xi \cdot \gamma _\varepsilon =\operatorname {vol}(\alpha +\varepsilon \omega ) -(t_0+\varepsilon )\omega \cdot \gamma _\varepsilon \leq ((n-1)\varepsilon -t_0)\omega \cdot \gamma _\varepsilon <0  \] when $(n-1)\varepsilon <t_0$. Since the pairing is continuous, a sufficiently late actual approximating single-power generator is still strictly negative against $\xi $. This proves $C^*\subset \mathcal E$. Finite-dimensional bipolarity now gives $C=\mathcal E^*$. For completeness, if a point $z$ lies outside a closed convex cone, choose its nearest point $c$ in an auxiliary Euclidean norm. A minimum exists by compactness after restricting to a sufficiently large ball. The first-variation inequality and the choices $0,2c$ show that $\ell (w)=(c-z)\cdot w$ is nonnegative on the cone and $\ell (z)=-\| z-c\| ^2<0$. The perfect pairing represents this separating linear functional, which proves the bipolar assertion. Finally $C\subset \mathcal M\subset \mathcal E^*=C$, proving all claims. $\square$
